newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end little-changed before data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end little-changed before data.

text.p: Pre-employment report jitters cut into trading volume on Thursday in U.S. debt futures, leaving the market mixed but little-changed on the day.
September Treasury bond futures drifted narrowly during the latter part of the day, tied to a tight range between 109-28/32 and 110-02/32 from late morning into the close.
Some brokers noted signs early of yield-curve-steepening trades, as players bought the short end and sold the long end.
"I heard about buying the twos (two year notes) and selling bonds, but that was early," said a T-bond futures broker. "I haven't heard anything since."
Late activity picked up again in the short end, however, with traders seeing size dealer selling concentrated in September Eurodollar futures, which edged off in the final minutes.
"There was some good-volume selling, especially in the Septembers," one Eurodollar floor broker said.
He also noted selling of volatility in the Eurodollar options pit as options traders weighed whether Friday's May U.S. non-farm payrolls report will jar the market much and decided it might not.
Some brokers figured the upside in debt futures will be limited unless nonfarm payrolls shows remarkable weakness.
They said a soft payrolls figures might be brushed aside as a function of the government's revision of seasonal factors.

Economists, on average, following the announcement of the revisions looked for nonfarm payrolls to rise 219,000, with a 5.0-percent jobless rate, a 0.4-percent gain in average hourly earnings and an average workweek of 34.7 hours.
On the other hand, some said strong payrolls growth might be viewed in conjunction with signs that retail-level demand is trailing off somewhat, which could mitigate any downside response.
In the long end, brokers said many players stood aside, continuing the trend of the last couple of sessions that saw open interest drop some 35,000 in T-bond futures.

Futures showed limited response to the unexpected rise in weekly U.S. jobless claims. Futures slipped overnight after Richmond Federal Reserve Bank President Alfred Broaddus said he did not know if interest rates were high enough to moderate growth to a longterm sustainable level.
Sept T-bonds lost 1/32 to 110-00, notes rose 1/32 107-27/32, munis rose 6/32 to 116-08/32, Sept bills were flat at 94.650, Dec Eurodollars lost 0.005 to 93.790.
